title: Blazer Millie
text: “Punishment complete! Wait for the judgment of Melromarc, ruler of all the land!”
“This is the victory of love, courage, and justice!”
The queen and Fleon-chan were delivering their victory speech, I say. But then the queen quickly scanned the surroundings. And locked eyes with the Filolial-masked whatever-he-was.
“Well done, Blazer Millie. I’ll always be watching over you. Farewell!”
In a flash, accompanied by light—what looked like a teleportation skill—the Filolial mask’s figure vanished!
“…There is still much evil left in this country. I cannot linger here. Let us go.”
“Yes! Love and courage’s Blazer Fleon, alongside Blazer Millie, shall smite evil aboard the Basher Machine—”

With a flap, the queen mounted Fleon-chan’s back and swiftly took to the sky… and when I squinted, I saw her land quickly some distance away and come running back. Her outfit was back to her usual attire.
“I heard what sounded like screams, so I came to see—this is—”
“Ah, yes.”
The queen bound the fallen bandits with an extra layer of ice magic to make sure they couldn’t move, then went to check on the villagers.
“Forgive my belated introduction. I am the queen of this nation, Melromarc. These men appear to be bandits who have wronged you. I intend to take them into custody—is that acceptable?”
“Eh… ah, Queen, Your Majesty! Please, I beg you to do so!”

The queen made her proposal without making the villager feel the weight of their difference in status, and the villager, perhaps overwhelmed, bowed deeply in gratitude. A procession of knights who seemed to be her retainers went about binding the bandits. We watched from a distance, careful not to be noticed… but Father wasn’t even watching the scene anymore. What was wrong with him, I wondered?
“…Let’s go home.”
Father murmured that quietly.
“Home it is! Understood!”
“Going home, nano.”

Rival let out what sounded like a deflated sigh. The queen seemed to be putting on some show with that tailcoat fellow that I didn’t quite understand. But it’s me who fights in Filolial-sama’s mask, I say!
“Ah… I understand a lot of things now. Including the reason for her running away from home.”
Crocodile Guy and Rabbit Guy also trudged back over, looking worn out. It seemed that was the reason behind Fiancée’s running away.
“Well, this is Melromarc. There’s no need for us to butt in here.”
“Yeah… if we crash in there, we’d probably end up cast as the monster-of-the-week, so our objectives are different anyway.”
And so, Father headed home, chatting with Crocodile Guy and the others. It seemed Father and the rest had figured something out.
And so we arrived in front of the mansion where Fiancée was staying. After explaining the situation to Éclair, we ended up discussing what to do about it in the garden.
“The queen and the others did something like that…”
Éclair seemed to be choosing her words carefully.
“Well, it’s possible this town will end up seeing quite enough of it too, before long.”
“Hmm… as a knight of this nation, I’m not in a position to raise objections against the queen’s peacekeeping activities, but… is it really that unbearable to watch?”
“Well… some people might be fine with it, but if I’m honest, Melty-chan found it pretty hard to stomach. So? Don’t you think it’s about time you came out? Rafumi-chan?”
“Fufufu… you called, did you?”
“Come out even if nobody called you, nano.”
With a rustle, Rafumi poked her face out. Ren came along too, reluctantly.
“Looks like you came to check things out.”
“Ah, well, yeah… so? Was it Rafumi-chan who was behind this after all?”
“Being called the culprit is rather insulting. I simply thought it wasn’t right to leave the maintenance of this nation’s public order entirely to Azott and me, so I did various things as a result.”
“That’s certainly one way to put it… though it’s also true the decline in public order here has been pretty severe.”
Father lamented just how many bandits, brigands, and thieves had multiplied around here.
“So why did it end up turning into that?”
“What do you think? A new hero, a new presence like Melfilo, so to speak.”
“I feel like, motif-wise, Melfilo isn’t really ‘new’ so much as… an ancestor, or more like a grandmother-tier generation gap…”
The ‘blazer’ part is clearly intentional, Father added.

“Well, it’s another world, so magical girls being a thing isn’t exactly surprising… but given it’s treated like a beautiful-girl-warrior ranger squad, maybe it’s meant to be a return to the genre’s roots? Hmm.”
Apparently, genre-wise, what they’d been rampaging around doing was treated as something fresh and new, even though it was actually older than the Melfilo act that Fiancée and Filo-tan sometimes did.
“There are remakes of old works and all, but even so, I feel like this is pushing it a bit. I hear the queen’s actually fairly young, but even so, I think this is a rough position to put her in.”
“I won’t deny that someone should tell her to think about her age.”
Ren muttered, looking away.
“If you knew, shouldn’t you have stopped it?”
“By the time I saw it, it was already in full swing. Was I supposed to jump into that circle?”
Rabbit Guy and Crocodile Guy looked away without saying anything at Ren’s words. There seemed to be an atmosphere that made it impossible to interject.

“And on top of that, it was right in the middle of the happy married couple gazing into each other’s eyes, you know? You want me to jump in there and tell them to stop? On what grounds? If they talk back, I’ve got nothing to say. Naofumi, could you do it?”
Father looked away too.
“Fine, I get it, but I still think this is the kind of pattern where you should’ve stopped it right at the start…”
“There’ve been similar loops before, so I can sort of imagine how it played out, nano, but why did it end up like that, nano?”
“Heh… I gave it a push, but I wasn’t involved all that deeply, was I?”

Rafumi grinned and then explained the circumstances. Even so, much like the loop where the Crimson Swine had been mistaken for dead as the culprit, turning Trash into Filolial Cross, it seems the whole thing started when Fleon-chan noticed Trash agonizing over something while he was living a peaceful life at the castle with Tiger Girl and the others, and went to talk to him.
“I can feel it, clear as day! The hesitation in your heart, unable to just sit still and do nothing! So let’s be heroes together!”

It seemed to be yet another one of Fleon-chan’s many attempts at recruiting Trash. Apparently she’d timed it for when Fiancée and Tiger Girl weren’t around. Incidentally, Kuro-chan was apparently off playing with a different Rafumi and wasn’t present for this.

“I’m sorry, but it is because of me that this nation suffered such terrible damage… who would have thought the darkness of this country would swell so much that the heroes themselves had to pass judgment upon it. All of this is because of my own hatred.”

Something about how Trash, who had once sympathized with Three Heroes Church’s policy of hating demi-humans and beastmen, had witnessed footage of the horrific abuse committed by the Church firsthand and felt responsible for the judgment Itsuki had been forced to carry out. Apparently, thanks to Trash’s own “great achievements,” the notion that demi-humans and beastmen were an evil to be defeated had thoroughly permeated Melromarc, and it had led to the conclusion that, with Trash as its figurehead, the world would eventually be unified, and with Shield Hero at the forefront, the extermination of demi-humans and beastmen would be carried out. And yet, apparently, Trash had also come to realize—not that meeting Tiger Girl had changed his heart exactly, but that his hatred hadn’t run quite that deep to begin with. He hated them, yes, but there had still been enough conscience left in him to stop short at witnessing the torture firsthand. The idea that he himself bore responsibility for turning this country into one devoid of conscience was apparently the source of his endless brooding.
“I have no right…”
This time, it seemed the queen had been present.
“Eh… Fleon-san. I’m aware you’ve been coming to consult with my husband, but could you please leave now…”

While the queen, choosing her words carefully, was trying to get Fleon-chan to go home, Rafumi—disguised as Ren—apparently stepped up beside Fleon-chan and made her proposal with a bold, confident smirk.

“Heh… will just smoldering here do the world even the slightest bit of good? If we leave the waves of catastrophe entirely to the heroes, do you really think this apocalyptic, end-of-days state of affairs will turn out for the better? No matter how much support I have, there’s a limit to how much I alone can resolve a situation like this.”
“I understand what you’re saying, but…”
“Then, Queen, you’re saying it’s fine to leave things as they are?”
“That’s not what I—”
Faced with the words of Rafumi in disguise, the queen found herself unable to continue.
